newsitem.title: UK: Fashanu will not testify in soccer bribes trial.
newsitem.headline: Fashanu will not testify in soccer bribes trial.

text.p: Former Wimbledon striker John Fashanu will not give evidence to a trial in which he is charged with helping to fix top-level English soccer matches, his lawyer told a court on Thursday.
"He will exercise his absolute right of silence consistent with the attitude he adopted when the police arrested him in the glare of publicity several years ago," lawyer Trevor Burke said.

Fashanu and Malaysian businessman Heng Suan Lim are charged with paying former Liverpool goalkeeper Bruce Grobbelaar and one-time Wimbledon keeper Hans Segers to rig matches on behalf of an Asian betting syndicate. All four have pleaded not guilty.
Defendants in English trials are under no obligation to testify or allow themselves to be cross-examined. Burke said the only words Fashanu had uttered since being charged were "Not guilty".

"Any experienced policeman or prosecutor knows those two important words convey one message to those who prosecute him -- Prove it if you can' -- and that is exactly what John Fashanu invites them to do," Burke said.
"You have brought him here, you prove it if you can."
